memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Abel kept flocks, and Cain worked the soil. In the course of time Cain brought some of the fruits of the soil as an offering to the Lord. And Abel brought fat portions from some of the firstborn of his flock. - Gen 4:2b-4a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two brothers, two jobs, two offerings. On the surface this looks simple - one farmed, one kept sheep, and both brought something to God. But look closely at the words. Cain brought "some of the fruits." Abel brought "fat portions" from the "firstborn." One gave leftovers; the other gave his best and his first.

The difference wasn't the type of offering, but the heart behind it. Abel gave in a way that said God deserved the finest he had. Cain gave in a way that said God could have whatever was left over.

We do the same today. We can give God our leftover time, our tired attention, our spare change - or we can give Him our first and our best. God does not need our gifts, but He sees what our giving reveals about our love for Him.

The good news is that our offerings are never the basis of our acceptance. In Christ, we come to God accepted already, and then we give our best out of gratitude, not to earn His favour (Rom 12:1).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you giving God your first, or only your leftovers?
- What does your giving reveal about your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for the times I have offered You only what was left over. Help me give You my first and my best, because You are worthy.
